note: Hand-curated calibration, kept OUT of proto_catalog.json because that file is regenerated from proto-tools on every `litkb proto-sync` and everything in it is derived. Keyed by (tool, metric): one model emits several metrics and may be characterised for some and not others. Overlaid at build time by proto.apply_calibration. Tool-level `status` is DERIVED from these, never curated.
promotion_rule: A metric becomes "validated" only on measured reliability against a held-out benchmark, per docs/PRD-framework.md section 6, and the record must carry `measured_error` and `benchmark` or it is refused. Absence means needs_calibration; silence is never a promotion.
known_gaps: Section 6 requires measured error per evaluator (so no design margin is claimed finer than it) and an applicability domain (so out-of-domain candidates are flagged and excluded from ranking). Both fields are demonstrated on the `example` block below, not on any curated record here -- `tools` is still `{}`. `measured_error` is now read: formulation_agent007/validate.py's margin check rejects a gate whose threshold, or `between` window, is finer than the measured error of a metric validated for the tools that gate names, and emit.py labels any gate that is not fully calibrated in the runbook. `applicability_domain` is still recorded but not enforced against anything: there is no candidate set yet to check it against.
Only 48 of 140 catalogued tools emit metrics at all; the other 92 are generators, retrievers, aligners and annotators for which calibration is meaningless. The real calibration surface is those 48.

Nothing distinguishes a curator from anyone with write access to this file. `apply_calibration` checks that a `validated` record is well-formed -- a positive numeric `measured_error.value` and a `benchmark` -- but enforces no authority check on who supplies it. Framework section 11 Q5 leaves 'who may promote' open, and a promotion here changes what the whole system is permitted to claim.
